summary: The shared shadow predicate excluded protocol_members wholesale, so a Protocol body's `def x` failed to shadow an inherited class attribute and `C.x` folded the base's constant instead of CPython's function object.
note: Confirmed by measurement before fixing: for `class P(Protocol): def x(self) -> int: ...` / `class A: x: int = 2` / `class C(P, A)`, CPython printed the function object while pycc printed 2. Both crates agreed on the wrong value, so the shared-predicate guard could not catch it. The exclusion is narrowed to ProtocolMember::Attribute; ProtocolMember::Method now shadows and the read stays T0044. Pinned by tests/issue_974_inherited_class_attr_by_class_name.rs::a_protocol_method_member_shadows_an_inherited_class_attribute; the pre-existing positive test was renamed to name its Attribute half.

summary: The #974 sentence listed four of the five shadow namespaces the predicate checks, omitting enum members, while docs/TYPE_SYSTEM.md listed all of them.
note: The sentence now lists methods, @staticmethod, @classmethod, @property, enum members and a Protocol-body def. The explanatory prose was deliberately not added: docs/ROADMAP.md had 81 bytes of headroom under scripts/check-site.sh's 168960-byte llms.txt budget, and the owning specification docs/TYPE_SYSTEM.md carries the reasoning.

summary: The class-name read bullet described the MRO walk unconditionally, without disclosing that a PEP 695 generic class accepts the read under `pycc check` and then fails `pycc build` with T0021.
note: The divergence predates #974 (an own-declared class attribute on a generic class already diverged the same way) and is item 3 of follow-up issue #989, which is why this change's test matrix carries no PEP 695 case. The bullet now states the exception inline and cites #989.

summary: The #436 class-name AttrGet arm fired whenever env.lookup_class(name) succeeded, without checking whether an active value binding shadows that name, so a parameter named after a class read the class attribute instead of the parameter's instance slot
note: Codex P1 on PR #992, thread PRRT_kwDOTiOo7s6f7GJ3. Measured against CPython 3.13.9: the inherited shape was a regression this PR introduced (base 3ba4a027 gave T0044, HEAD gave 2, CPython gives 3); the own-declared shape was pre-existing (base already gave 2); the enum-member shape was pre-existing (base gave T0022). Fixed with the binding_state/is_local guard the class-name Subscript path already used, placed before the whole block so all three shapes are covered at once.

summary: The MIR class-attribute fold and the enum-member interception both gated only on classes.get/try_lower_enum_member_attr, so guarding pycc_types alone would have sent a shadowed class name through the instance path and into the fold's internal-error panic
note: Not raised by Codex; found while mirroring the pycc_types guard. The enum-member site was demonstrably reachable: after guarding only the class-attribute fold, the enum repro type-checked and then failed LLVM module verification (ret ptr from an i64 function). Both sites now consult the active scopes, the spelling the __class_getitem__ interception in the same file already used.

summary: The class-name `MethodCall` arm resolved `B.m()` through the class's static/class-method tables without checking for an active value binding of `B`, so a parameter named after a class was ignored: measured CPython 3.13.9 prints 3, pycc printed 2, for both a @staticmethod and a @classmethod carrier. Found by probing the same defect class at a fourth site after the AttrGet guard landed; the MIR class-name method-call interception needed the mirroring scopes guard too.
note: Fixed by the same binding_state/is_local pair placed before the method-table walk, plus the MIR scopes guard. Two tests added (static and class method carriers). The TYPE_SYSTEM.md and ROADMAP.md sentences enumerating the guard's reach were widened from three shapes to four in the same commit, since shipping them at three would have stated a rule with a known counterexample.

summary: P2 (Codex, PR #992): rewrite_generic_calls_in_expr recursed into the base of an AttrGet/MethodCall unconditionally, so with any PEP 695 generic function declared in the module a bare class name reached infer_expr_in as a value and failed with T0021. Measured pre-existing rather than a #974 regression: `A.X` (own attribute) and `A.m()` (static method) failed identically without any inherited read involved.
note: Fixed by the same skip the file's own Subscript (__class_getitem__) arm already applied, extracted into a shared is_class_name_base helper and applied at all three sites; the helper carries the binding_state/is_local pair so an active binding still shadows the class inside a generic module. Five CLI tests (inherited attribute, own attribute, static method, class method, shadowed method) plus two crate-internal tests in pycc_types::tests, which the coverage gate required: the CLI tests land in a different instantiation record of rewrite_generic_calls_in_expr than the crate's own unit-test build, and llvm-cov takes the per-function minimum across records. The Slice arm was probed and provably needs no branch -- `A[1:2]` on a class name is rejected with T0021 by the checker itself, with or without a generic in the module. TYPE_SYSTEM.md and ROADMAP.md widened in the same round.

summary: P1 (Codex, PR #992): the round-2/3 shadowing guard asks binding_state against the environment as it stands after ALL top-level code has run whenever it runs inside a function body (D-041 late binding, module.rs pass 3), so a module-level rebinding of a class's own name is resolved ordering-blind. Measured against CPython 3.13.9 across four programs: with `A = D()` after the call CPython prints 2 and with it before the call CPython prints 1, from a compile-time environment that is identical in both. origin/main 7bc37e03 printed 2 for both (wrong on the second row); the round-2 guard made the branch print 1 for both (wrong on the first) -- the P1 was correct, and probing it found the extra row the report did not have.
note: Fixed by rejecting the ambiguous read with C0001 rather than resolving it either way; ordering-aware name resolution is a separate analysis this compiler does not have. A first attempt rejected the *rebinding statement* in module.rs pass 2 and was refuted by an existing test (a_value_binding_shadowing_a_class_name_indexes_as_a_value): pass 2 walks top-level statements in source order, so module scope is already sound and a rejection there removes a working capability. The landed fix is narrow -- Environment::in_function_body, set only by child_for_function, distinguishes the two positions, and the three dispatch sites (Subscript, AttrGet, MethodCall) route through one shared expr::class_name_dispatch predicate. Parameter and function-local shadows are untouched, pinned by a dedicated test plus the two pre-existing subscript tests that stayed green unedited. pycc_mir needs no branch: the checker rejects before MIR runs. Seven crate-internal tests (one per dispatch site's Err path plus the four measured rows and the parameter pin) and four CLI tests.
